projects.title: Myrtle
projects.description: A private pipeline for capturing how someone writes and extending it.

projects.title: Scribbles
projects.description: More and more, documents get reviewed by people and AI assistants at the same time — and that gets messy fast. Scribbles keeps it all in one place: comments, suggested edits, replies, and version history that never get lost when you refresh. It's built so an AI assistant can read and comment on a document directly, instead of me copy-pasting back and forth.
features: Inline comments and suggested edits that stay pinned to the right spot
Accept or reject each suggestion with one click
Replies, resolve and reopen, filters, and a minimap for long documents
Full version history with one-click restore
Autosaves as you type, with draft recovery if something goes wrong
Built for AI assistants to review documents directly — no browser needed
Export and share documents as portable files
Runs entirely on your own machine

projects.title: NHL Watcher
projects.description: I'm a Leafs fan who can't keep up with every NHL podcast, so I built NHL Watcher to do it for me. It monitors notable hockey podcasts and shows, transcribes them, detects Leafs-related topics, and clusters the coverage into a ranked topic board — so I can see what everyone's talking about, with short quotes, timestamps, and links back to the original episode.
features: Monitors NHL podcasts, YouTube shows, and radio reposts automatically
Transcribes full episodes and detects Leafs-related topics
Clusters coverage into ranked topic threads across sources
Ranks topics by source diversity, mention count, discussion time, and recency
Short quotes with speaker attribution, sentiment, and timestamps
Public, no-login topic board; full transcripts stay private
FastAPI backend and Next.js UI, deployed on Railway with cron polling

projects.title: CC Demos
projects.description: Claude ships new features constantly, but most land as a changelog line nobody pictures themselves using. CC Demos is an automated pipeline that turns each new Claude Code feature into a polished ~20-second vertical video — AI-narrated, with a BEFORE/NOW story and three concrete use cases. One feature description goes in, a finished, shareable demo comes out.
features: One feature in → one finished demo video out, fully hands-off
BEFORE/NOW story structure rendered programmatically with Remotion
AI-narrated voiceover via ElevenLabs text-to-speech
Three named, concrete use cases per feature — no generic filler
Vertical 9:16 format for X, YouTube Shorts, and Reels
Combine step joins feature videos into one reel without re-rendering
Triggered by a /cc-demos slash command or a single npm script

projects.title: Sally Sold
projects.description: Most invoicing tools are bloated with features freelancers don't need. Sally Sold strips it down to the essentials — fill in the details, pick a template, and download a stunning PDF. Your first invoice takes under 60 seconds.
features: 6 designer templates — Studio, Mono, Craft, Noir, Ledger, Bold
4-step wizard: line items, your details, client, preview and download
Accent color picker to match your brand
PDF generation with pixel-perfect fidelity
Save your business details and client list for repeat invoices
Invoice history with re-download and duplicate

projects.title: Asoona
projects.description: Asoona is a self-hosted, AI-first Asana replacement. Built with a REST API that Claude Code queries directly. Each project has a bottleneck indicator. External services can create tasks via inbound webhooks.
features: Drag-and-drop kanban board with customizable columns
Project status headers (objective, where I left off, bottleneck)
Full REST API for programmatic task management
Portfolio and list views with filtering and sorting
Custom fields and automation rules per project
SQLite-backed with real-time optimistic updates via SWR
Trash and restore for deleted tasks

projects.title: Dev Proxy
projects.description: I got tired of remembering which localhost port belongs to which project. Dev Proxy is a local reverse proxy I built from scratch — it routes .test domains to my dev servers so I can just type asoona.test or beautiful-invoices.test instead of localhost:3741. A dashboard at dev.test shows what's running and lets me start or stop servers with a toggle.
features: Custom reverse proxy with dnsmasq for automatic .test domain resolution
Dashboard at dev.test showing all projects with live status indicators
Toggle switches to start and stop dev servers from the browser
Auto-restart for crashed dev servers with configurable retry limits
Registry-based port management — no more port conflicts
Auto-detects archived projects and hides them from the dashboard
Starts on boot via macOS launchd — zero maintenance
Self-restarts when source code changes, no manual deploys

projects.title: Custom Superpowers
projects.description: I forked the superpowers plugin, built a simulated panel of Anthropic engineers including Claude Code's creator, and had them redesign the plugin to account for the newly released 1M context window.
features: Simulated Anthropic advisory panel (Boris Cherny + 5 team members) guided the redesign
14 skills consolidated to 7 — merged redundant workflows, removed context-conservation overhead
Philosophy shift: use the context window fully, subagents only for true parallelism
Continuous verification after every step, not just at completion
Dual-layer communication — plain language for the user, technical details for the code

projects.title: PFIN
projects.description: I built PFIN to make sense of my spending across multiple currencies and bank accounts. It processes bank statements from different sources, auto-categorizes transactions, and generates monthly summaries so I can see exactly where my money goes.
features: Multi-currency support (USD, CAD, IDR) with unified reporting
Bank statement PDF parsing from multiple institutions
Automatic transaction categorization by merchant and pattern
Monthly spending summaries with category breakdowns
Financial goal tracker with visual progress dashboard
Smart duplicate detection and self-transfer exclusion
Handles Wise, traditional banks, and credit card statements

projects.title: Fling
projects.description: Fling is a single-purpose iOS app for getting thoughts out of your head as fast as possible. You open it, type or dictate, swipe up, and the note saves as a Markdown file to iCloud Drive, a Files folder, or an automation webhook.
features: Swipe-up gesture to instantly save notes as Markdown files
iCloud Drive default destination with local fallback
Configurable save location via iOS folder picker
Optional webhook delivery through verified connection links
Voice dictation with live transcription
Security-scoped bookmarks for persistent folder access
Pure SwiftUI, no third-party dependencies

projects.title: HealthDash
projects.description: I wanted a single dashboard for all my Garmin health data without relying on the Garmin Connect app. HealthDash pulls metrics from my Garmin watch daily via an automated pipeline and renders everything in a static HTML dashboard I can open anytime.
features: Automated daily data collection from Garmin Connect API
Static HTML dashboard with no server required
Sleep analysis with duration, stages, and trend tracking
Heart health metrics including resting HR, HRV, and VO2 max
Activity tracking with steps, calories, and workout history
Body composition trends (weight, hydration, respiration)
macOS launchd integration for hands-free daily updates

projects.title: Copy Jamie
projects.description: I built copyjamie.com as the foundation for my email copywriting portfolio. It's a static site with no framework — just clean HTML, CSS, and a touch of JavaScript. The actual email portfolio hasn't been added yet, but the site is live and designed to load fast, look sharp, and let the writing speak for itself.
features: Static HTML/CSS site hosted on a custom domain
Responsive design that works across all devices
Contact page with a clean inquiry form
Privacy policy page for GDPR compliance
Custom favicon set (SVG, PNG, ICO)
Open Graph meta tags for social sharing
Zero dependencies, instant load times

projects.title: Bookwise
projects.description: I built Bookwise because I wanted my Kindle highlights to feel alive, not buried in a file I never open. It imports my highlights and surfaces them in daily review sessions with spaced repetition — 7 highlights per session, weighted toward what I haven't seen in a while. I can star what resonates and add notes during review.
features: Daily review sessions with spaced repetition across 11,000+ highlights
Immersive full-screen review UI with warm serif typography and crossfade transitions
Star and annotate highlights during review — annotations persist in book detail view
Book covers auto-fetched from Open Library API
Want to Read list with Amazon links and recommendation notes
Import from Kindle clippings and Readwise CSV exports
SQLite-backed durable storage with IndexedDB as fast local cache

projects.title: Personal Dictation
projects.description: I was paying for WisprFlow just to dictate text. Personal Dictation is a local-only macOS replacement — hold Right Option, speak, release, and the text appears wherever your cursor is. Everything runs on-device with mlx-whisper, so nothing leaves my machine.
features: Hold-to-talk — hold Right Option, speak, release
Local-only transcription via mlx-whisper (~190ms)
Text appears in any focused app automatically
Animated neon purple waveform during recording
Transcription history with search and copy
Auto-launches on login, restarts if it crashes
Sound feedback confirms press and release
